page: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine within the general-purpose Daldsv7 family, tailored for compute-intensive workloads that require lower memory footprints per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz. The instance allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores via Microsoft Hyper-V, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, SHA extensions, and AES cryptography.

The instance includes 32 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features an integrated 945 GB local NVMe SSD alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The local NVMe disk provides high-speed, temporary scratch storage directly attached to the host, reducing latency for local read and write operations. The instance does not feature dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-core execution speed. In stress-ng single-core tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core evaluations, the D16alds_v7 performs in the top ten percent of evaluated instances. Multi-core compute performance, memory bandwidth, and static web serving throughput register in the median tier. Text generation latency on smaller language models also places in the top tier due to high single-thread clock frequencies.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the reduced memory footprint provides a resource-dense configuration for tasks that prioritize CPU frequency over memory scale. The inclusion of bundled NVMe storage further enhances efficiency by eliminating the immediate need for auxiliary caching disks. It is particularly well-suited for batch compute, code compilation, CI/CD runners, web serving, and compression pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v7 is an execution-focused virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor capable of clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance provides 32 GB of system memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. A bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD delivers fast scratch storage, while standard GPU acceleration is absent. Performance benchmarks show top-tier results in single-threaded tasks, including gzip compression and Geekbench single-core execution, complemented by steady mid-tier multi-core output. The hardware balance makes the D16alds_v7 cost-effective for CPU-dominated workloads that do not demand extensive RAM capacity. Key suitable applications include software compilation, web serving, continuous integration runners, data compression pipelines, and light machine learning inference.
